text:
maya: Quick sync — we need to settle the on‑prem/VPC launch gates and upgrade lanes for the customer-managed networking asks hitting us. I sketched a proposal below. cc @zoe @liam

liam: TL;DR?

maya: Proposal: three minimum acceptance criteria for GA: 1) Installer supports 'customer-managed network' mode that requires zero manual ip rewrites for basic topologies. 2) Upgrade path: minor patch upgrades can be staged with <1h nominal downtime for 3-node clusters; major upgrades require a canary + rollback plan. 3) Handoff: network runbook + automated sanity checks (BGP/peering and egress IP validation) included in delivery.

zoe: +1 on runbook. Need explicit tests for NAT/dual-stack. Customers keep hitting NAT hairpins. Also need a clear statement about static egress IP preservation.

sam: For the installer, can we add a mode flag? e.g.
```
redwood-install --mode onprem --network customer-managed --preserve-egress true
```
That would let field validate preflight and abort early.

liam: This feels close. Two negotiable items: SLA on upgrade downtime, and whether we require operator-side BGP or support a relay option for NAT-only customers. Product prefers relay as lower lift. Ops prefers BGP for predictability.

zoe: Relay is okay for small customers, but for enterprise customers we must certify BGP peering + route filtering. Otherwise netops will refuse.

maya: Suggestion: define launch slices. Slice A = small customers (relay allowed, minimal runbook), Slice B = mid/enterprise (certified BGP + egress preservation + audit logs). Gate for Slice B: passed e2e lab peering test and at least two pilot customers.

liam: Agree. What's the rollout acceptance criteria for Slice A?

maya: Slice A acceptance: installer mode works end‑to‑end, preflight detects common misconfigs, upgrade dry-run succeeds on staging, documented fallback to relay. Also a short customer-facing checklist.

sam: Implementation note: preflight should include these checks: DNS resolution to controlplane, BGP session up (if requested), egress IP match, firewall rules. I can draft the checks.

zoe: Can we add an automated validation step for egress IP mapping? Lots of customers inject SNAT rules that break our KV-store reachability. If we detect mismatch, installer warns and suggests NAT rule example.

maya: Good. We'll include a snippet in the runbook. Example NAT rule we can recommend:
```
# preserve source IP for control-plane traffic
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -j SNAT --to-source <EGRESS_IP>
```
Include variations for cloud onramps.

liam: On upgrades: we need telemetry hooks so we can detect regressions in token latency for hosted fallbacks. Add that to ops checklist.

maya: Noted. Also: customer legal/contract ask — some customers want explicit IP retention guarantees in SOW. That affects our comms. 

zoe: If we promise IP retention, we should define allowed maintenance windows and a documented rollback SLA.

sam: Timeline ask: can eng deliver the preflight + installer flag by the end of next sprint? It's ~2 wks of work assuming no surprises.

liam: Product can sequence Slice A GA after that sprint + 1 week of pilot. So 3 weeks from now if all green.

maya: Okay — action items:
- sam: draft preflight checks + stub CLI flags (due +9d)
- zoe: draft runbook skeleton + egress validation guidance (due +9d)
- liam: prepare customer comm template and pilot criteria (due +11d)
- maya: assemble launch gate doc and SOW language (due +11d)

deploy-bot: New ticket created: #PRIVDEP-4891 "preflight checks for customer-managed networking" :white_check_mark:

zoe: I'll chat with field ops tomorrow to pick pilot candidates.

sam: I'll push a WIP branch with the flag and a dry-run check tomorrow.

liam: Sounds good. Circle back in the weekly launch sync. :thumbsup:
